natural_body: Price-sensitive SMBs: 40% off drove signup +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent archived records (memory_31, memory_86) converge on simplifying/shortening onboarding as a durable lever for activation without noted retention harm—directly addressing the observed decline while supporting the long-term qualified revenue objective. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure on price-sensitive SMBs, but its own record shows a 12% retention hit alongside revenue gains, which conflicts with 'sustainable long-term' framing; I want to verify that record before ruling it out entirely, and also verify one onboarding memory to confirm the consolidated claim isn't overstated or duplicative across two summaries. Given only one experiment slot this week, I'm prioritizing the funnel fix over a pricing race-to-the-bottom that risks eroding qualified revenue quality. Scale is standard rather than broad given competing signals and the need to confirm verified sources before wider commitment.
